races.title: State Assembly, District 9
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Matthew Adams
cands.bio: Educator and community organizer from Lodi. He has taught middle and high school math, science and social studies, and worked as a Regional Field Organizer for Equality California in the Central Valley. He has not held elected office. Democratic candidate for Assembly District 9.
cands.gaps: We found no record of where Adams was raised beyond his Lodi birthplace and Lodi High School. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or abortion. His housing comments (affordable housing, tenant protections, "smart, sustainable growth" and holding developers accountable) were too general to count as a position on slowing growth. His education comments (more K-12 funding, smaller classes, support for teachers) did not address school choice or a specific teacher pay raise. We found no reporting on controversies and no documented foreign ties. His campaign website's priorities and media pages were not available to us, so only its home page was read.

cands.name: Heath Flora
cands.bio: Republican Assemblymember for District 9 (northern San Joaquin Valley), first elected in 2016. Farmer and owner of Golden Valley Equipment, and a volunteer firefighter for over 15 years. He served as Assembly Minority Leader from September 2025 to August 2026.

controversies.text: In 2025 the Sacramento Bee reported that Flora registered to vote at his parents' Modesto property, where a relative's wife lives, while apparently living in Sacramento. That address let him collect tax-free per diem, $42,416 in 2024. No official finding has been reported. Flora has not commented in the stories.

The Sacramento Bee found Flora spent $606,213 of campaign money in 2024, a large share on travel, lodging and meals. Many Sacramento restaurant and bar charges were labeled "district meetings" but fell on weekends or recess, outside his district. The California Post reported state ethics probes. Flora has not commented.

In July 2022 a lobbyist for the California Medical Association, Emily Hughes, said publicly that she had an affair with Flora while he sat on the Assembly Health Committee. Flora said he would issue a statement but had not by the time of the report. He didn't say whether he recused himself on medical association bills.

Court documents reported by the Sacramento Bee show Flora agreed in June 2023 to pay $2,000 a month in child support. Two months later his ex-wife's lawyer asked the Assembly to withhold his pay for nonpayment. A San Joaquin County court later ordered over $16,000 in past-due support and uncovered healthcare costs.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; International Union of Operating Engineers Local 3; YIMBY Action (plus voter-guide recommendations from Based in Malibu and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Flora was raised or when he left Modesto for Ripon beyond the 2015 move. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, police funding, guns, abortion or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020 through 2026, and his campaign site has only general statements about forests, small business and agriculture. We found no documented stance on data centers or development. The controversy reports come from a Wikipedia summary that did not show its underlying news articles or any response from Flora. We did not find the details of the bills he sponsored.
